data.name: Fancy Skulls
data.detailed_description:
Fancy Skulls is a challenging first person shooter with procedural generation, permanent death and distinct art style.
Intense and tactical combat, unique weapon mods and items that change the way you play.


Foes different not only in visual design but also in their behavior. For example there is an enemy that will teleport every time you hit it, or enemy that leaves bombs that home on you, but you can shoot those bombs to use them against it.



Usable items and power ups, like friendly sentry, an eye that lets you transmute items, kite that lets you fly, matchbox that ignites all foes around you, and much more!


Each weapon is different from another, and every weapon can be modded with options that provide interesting game experiences like "walk backwards to get ammo", "12 hits with no misses give you money", "last two bullets in a magazine do double damage", "don't spend ammo while in the air", "shoot lightning bolts with shotgun".

reviews.review:
Fancy Skulls is a strange first person shooter that I think is much more interesting because of how different it feels from a normal roguelike. I am moving through a series of randomly generated rooms, fighting weird skull creatures and other strange enemies while trying to survive a run without dying. The game takes place around a very abstract museum like setting, and everything from the enemies to the weapons has this bizarre art style that makes it feel almost like I am shooting at living pieces of modern art. It is an old game from 2014 and it was left in Early Access, so I can definitely see where the rough edges are, but there is still a good idea underneath everything.

The combat is much more deliberate than I expected. I have to watch what the enemies are doing because they do not all attack in the same way. Some enemies teleport when I damage them, while others leave bombs around the room that can actually become useful if I shoot them at the right time. I really like having to learn these behaviours instead of simply holding down the trigger and hoping everything dies. The game also gives me different weapons and strange upgrades, so one run can end up feeling quite different from another depending on what I find.

The weapon modifications are probably my favourite part. Each weapon can be changed with effects that completely alter how I use it, and some of the combinations are properly weird. I can get effects that reward me for walking backwards, give me extra money for accurate shots or change how ammunition works. There are also items that give me temporary abilities, including a friendly sentry, an item that can change other items, a kite that lets me fly and a matchbox that can ignite enemies around me. I like this because the game is not only about finding a stronger gun. I am also trying to work out what kind of setup I can build from the things I find.

The biggest issue for me is that Fancy Skulls never feels completely finished. There are nine levels with procedural rooms, but the overall amount of enemy and room variety is fairly limited once I have played enough runs. The game was released in Early Access and the developer has not updated it for many years, so I am basically playing it in the state it was left in. That matters because I can see the potential for something much bigger, but I never get that feeling that the game is properly building towards anything. I am getting interesting ideas one after another without enough content around them to make the whole experience feel complete.

I also think the challenge can become a little uneven. At first the enemies are interesting because I have to learn what they do, but once I understand their patterns some of the danger starts to disappear. There are also room rewards based around taking no damage, missing no shots and clearing enemies quickly, which gives me another reason to play carefully. I like the idea, although some of these extra challenges can feel more annoying than rewarding when I am already trying to survive a difficult room. The game is at its best when I am making decisions about weapons and positioning rather than chasing an arbitrary condition.

The visual style is probably going to be one of those things that either works for me or does not. I actually like how strange it is. The enemies look like bizarre art pieces rather than normal monsters, and the simple environments give everything a slightly unsettling atmosphere. It is not a technically impressive game anymore, but I think the abstract design has aged better than the graphics themselves. I also like that the game does not try to explain every strange thing I am seeing. A lot of the appeal comes from simply wondering what the next room is going to throw at me.

Overall, Fancy Skulls is a game I think is held back more by its unfinished state than by its basic ideas. I really like the unusual enemies, strange weapons, weapon modifications and the more careful style of combat, and there are some genuinely clever roguelike mechanics here. At the same time, nine levels, limited variety and the lack of continued development make it difficult for me to rate it alongside more complete games in the genre. It feels like I am looking at the remains of a really promising game rather than a fully realised one. There is enough here for me to enjoy a few runs and remember it afterwards, but I would have wanted much more content and polish before giving it a much higher score.

Rating: 7.5/10
